_meta: A cluster of N nodes and one update that starts at a single node, used to show why disseminating state by gossip (each informed node tells another each round) beats a single-source broadcast: gossip reaches everyone in O(log N) rounds with the send load spread across the cluster and no single point of failure, while a single source is a linear-time bottleneck that strands everyone if it dies mid-dissemination. When one node learns something -- a new config, a membership change, a cache invalidation -- every other node needs to hear it. The obvious way is for the origin to send it to each of the others. That makes the origin a bottleneck (it does all N-1 sends) and a single point of failure (if it dies partway through, the nodes it had not reached yet never hear the update, and no one else is spreading it). Gossip (epidemic dissemination) flips this: in each round every node that already has the update passes it to another node that does not. The count of informed nodes roughly doubles each round, so the whole cluster is covered in about log2(N) rounds instead of N-1; the sends are spread across all the informed nodes instead of piled on the origin; and because many nodes are spreading, the death of any one node -- including the origin -- barely slows it. The same total number of messages (N-1, one per node informed) is delivered either way; gossip just parallelizes and decentralizes them. n is the number of nodes; source is the node the update starts at. n and source are the fixture; the rounds to inform everyone, the per-node send load, the total messages, and the robustness to the source failing are computed under each strategy.
